title: Indium Phosphide Wafer Market Size to Hit USD 679.76 Million by 2035 | SNS Insider

title: SanDisk And Micron Had Their Run – This New 'Photonics' ETF Has 15 Triple-Digit Gainers Inside
author: Piero Cingari
description: A new photonics ETF (EUV) launched on May 6, 2026, focusing on optical interconnect technology for AI data centers. The fund holds 15 stocks already up over 100% year-to-date, driven by structural demand from hyperscaler capex and supply constraints in indium phosphide lasers. However, critics note the ETF's top holdings lean toward general semiconductor names rather than pure photonics plays, duplicating exposure available in broader semiconductor funds.

title: This Obscure AI Stock Is Up by Almost 6,000% Over the Past Year. Can It Go Higher?
author: Marc Guberti
description: AXT, a semiconductor wafer substrate manufacturer, has surged nearly 6,000% in the past year due to its indium phosphide wafers used in AI chips. However, the company's fundamentals don't match its valuation—revenue declined year-over-year, it's still unprofitable, and the stock trades at a stretched 38x price-to-sales ratio. While AXT controls 80-90% of the indium phosphide market and is gaining Tier-1 customers, the current valuation requires perfection to justify, making it a risky investment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While AXT has a compelling long-term opportunity in indium phosphide wafers and controls a dominant market position, the article emphasizes that current valuation is stretched (38x P/S) relative to fundamentals. Revenue declined year-over-year despite massive stock gains, the company is still unprofitable, and the stock requires perfection to justify its price. The neutral sentiment reflects both the opportunity and significant risk.
Nvidia is mentioned as the primary beneficiary of silicon wafers from TSMC for AI chips, indicating its dominant position in the AI chip market and continued reliance on established supply chains.
TSMC is highlighted as the preferred supplier of silicon wafers to Nvidia for AI chips, demonstrating its critical role in the AI infrastructure supply chain.

title: AXT Stock Stumbles After The Close: Here's Why
author: Adam Eckert
description: AXT announced a public offering of common stock to support its subsidiary Beijing Tongmei Xtal Technology Co. and increase indium phosphide substrate production capacity. The stock declined 6.50% in after-hours trading to $73.51, despite being up over 6,500% in the past year and 381% year-to-date.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The stock declined 6.50% in after-hours trading following the announcement of a public offering of common stock, which typically dilutes existing shareholders and signals potential near-term weakness despite the company's strong year-to-date performance.

title: CEO Sells 31,000 Shares of AXT Worth $1.4 Million
author: Will Healy
description: AXT CEO Morris S. Young sold 30,832 shares worth approximately $1.4 million on March 10, 2026, representing 1.35% of his total holdings. The sale appears to be profit-taking following the stock's extraordinary 2,758% gain over the past year, driven by increased demand for semiconductor substrates in AI data centers and resumed operations in China. Young retains over 2.3 million shares, suggesting continued confidence in the company.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite the CEO's share sale, the article frames this as routine profit-taking rather than a loss of confidence. The company benefits from strong tailwinds in AI-driven data centers, high-speed optical connectivity demand, and resumed China operations. The CEO's retention of 2.3+ million shares demonstrates continued confidence. The stock's 2,758% one-year gain and emerging opportunities suggest further upside potential.
